worked_solution:
The parametric equations of a horizontal hyperbola centered at the origin with Cartesian equation

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1
$$

are given by

$$
x=a\operatorname{sec}⁡t,\,y=b\operatorname{tan}⁡t,
$$

where $a$ and $b$ are positive constants.

The vertices of the hyperbola occur at $(\pm a,0).$ From the graph, we have that $(\sqrt{8},0)$ is a vertex of the hyperbola, so $a=\sqrt{8}.$

The asymptotes of a horizontal hyperbola are $y=\pm \frac{b}{a}x.$ In our case, the asymptotes are $y=\pm \frac{\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{8}}x,$ and so we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{b}{a} & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{8}} \\ \frac{b}{\sqrt{8}} & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{8}} \\ b & =\sqrt{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the parametric equations of the hyperbola are

$$
x=\sqrt{8}\operatorname{sec}⁡t,\,y=\sqrt{3}\operatorname{tan}⁡t.
$$
